clips.title: The story
paras: In Astranaar, Pelturas Whitemoon still seeks a cure for his daughter Relara. Elune's Tear eased her nightmares, but a fierce fever grips her. Orendil Broadleaf sends him south for cooling stardust among ancient night elven stones.

Pelturas Whitemoon keeps vigil beside his daughter, Relara, as a malignant illness burns through her. Elune's Tear brought her some relief from the nightmares, but the sickness remains. A fierce fever still racks her, beyond the reach of ordinary medicines. With the temple healers stretched thin, Pelturas turns to old remedies drawn from nature, hoping to save her life.

Orendil Broadleaf, an elder herbalist, points Pelturas toward the Ruins of Stardust, south across the river from Astranaar. Frosted, shimmering dust settles on the plants among the fallen marble columns and archways of this ancient kaldorei sanctuary. The powder, called stardust, has a natural chill strong enough to draw out unnatural heat. Pelturas hopes to grind it into a poultice and ease Relara's fever.

Water elementals and wildlife make gathering the frosted dust dangerous among the flooded stones. Elementals, corrupted or stirred by changes in Ashenvale's balance, surge around the sunken plazas where the bushes grow thickest. You wade into shallows that look calm, watching for ambushes from the murky depths. The sparkling bushes must yield enough clean dust to carry back to Astranaar.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Elune's Tear washed clear some of my daughter's sickness. Her nightmares are lessened and I thank the goddess for her blessing. But... Fever still rages within her.
Orendil told me of a frosted dust found among the Ruins of Stardust. Perhaps it will abate Relara's fever. Gather some of the dust, then please return to me.
The Ruins of Stardust lie to the south, friend. May Elune speed your journey.

clips.title: Progress
paras: Do you yet have the Stardust, friend?

clips.title: Completion
paras: You gathered the dust! I will create a poultice from these—it should bring down Relara's fever.
Thank you again, friend. Without your help, my child would surely perish.
